passage: The Year Nine online class in Santiago ran on video, and Rosa clicked the raise-hand button when she had a question. Mr. Diaz called on her after Tariq finished, and she asked her question without talking over anyone. When someone made a joke in the chat she used a smiling emoji rather than unmuting. Tariq, though, had gone quiet with his camera off. The teacher waited, but nothing. Rosa typed, "Tariq, are you there? 👍 if yes." A thumbs-up appeared a minute later, then a message: "Sorry, my connection froze!" Rosa thought how easily a quiet screen could be taken for something else.

qa.q: Which button did Rosa click when she had a question?
qa.a: She clicked the raise-hand button.

qa.q: What might Tariq have been feeling when he stayed silent?
qa.a: He was probably frustrated by the frozen connection, though shyness or losing interest were other possibilities. His later message says the connection froze.

qa.q: What small step helped when Tariq went quiet?
qa.a: Rosa typed a gentle check and asked for a thumbs-up if he was there. That gave him an easy way to answer.

qa.q: How might the teacher have seen Tariq's silence?
qa.a: The teacher couldn't tell if it was shyness, lag or disengagement, so they waited. Silence on video is ambiguous.

grounding: A teenager uses the raise-hand and chat tools to take turns, and silence in a video call is ambiguous.

passage: The computer lab at Sahyadri School was buzzing. Twenty students sat in rows for a guest talk on video from another city. Mohit clicked the raise-hand icon when the speaker asked for questions, then clicked mute when the lab door banged. The speaker called on him. He unmuted and asked his question clearly. Two rows behind, Sudha's raise-hand icon glowed, but she said nothing when named. The speaker paused. Was she shy, or had her audio failed? Mohit leaned over. "Sudha, want me to read it?" She nodded. He typed her question in the chat, and the speaker answered it warmly.

qa.q: How many students sat in the computer lab?
qa.a: Twenty students sat in rows.

qa.q: What might Sudha have been feeling when she said nothing after being named?
qa.a: She might be shy, or her audio might have failed, so it is hard to tell. She nodded at Mohit's offer, which suggests she wanted to be heard.

qa.q: What small step could help a student who is quiet after raising a hand?
qa.a: Offer to type or read the question in the chat, as Mohit did. That lets the person take part without speaking.

qa.q: How does the speaker see Sudha's silence?
qa.a: The speaker can only see a raised hand and no voice, so they can't tell what is wrong. They paused and waited.

grounding: A teenager uses the raise-hand and mute tools to take turns, and silence in a call may mean shyness or audio trouble.

passage:
Dear Kashish Ma'am,
I wanted to explain about today's online class. When you asked me a question, I didn't answer for a long time. I know it looked like I wasn't paying attention.
Actually, my internet was lagging, and your voice kept cutting out. I clicked the raise-hand button twice, but I don't think it showed on your screen.
Also, I get really shy speaking on video. When everyone's camera is on and it's silent, I freeze.
Could I type my answers in the chat sometimes? Or use the hand emoji when I want to talk?
Thank you for understanding.
Varun

qa.q: How many times did Varun click the raise-hand button?
qa.a: Twice.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling during the silence in the online class?
qa.a: Varun felt shy and frozen speaking on video, and frustrated by the lag.

qa.q: What did Varun suggest to make online class easier?
qa.a: Typing answers in the chat or using the hand emoji when wanting to talk.

qa.q: How might Kashish Ma'am have seen Varun's silence before the email?
qa.a: Kashish Ma'am might have thought Varun wasn't paying attention, not knowing about the lag and shyness.

grounding: In an email, a teenager explains silence in an online class as lag and shyness, and suggests digital tools to take turns.

passage:
"Imran, you know how online classes were? For me, the mute button was my best friend. I'd keep it on unless I had something to say.
But one day, Mr Ghosh asked me something, and I didn't answer. I was trying to unmute, but my laptop froze. He said, 'Rajni, if you're not interested, you can leave.' My face went hot.
After class, I emailed him. I said my laptop froze, and I had clicked the raise-hand button. He wrote back, 'Sorry. I couldn't tell on my side.'
After that, he started saying, 'If you're stuck, type a hand emoji in the chat.' So now I, Rajni, use the hand emoji every time."

qa.q: What did Mr Ghosh say to Rajni when the answer didn't come?
qa.a: "Rajni, if you're not interested, you can leave."

qa.q: What was Rajni feeling when Mr Ghosh spoke to her like that?
qa.a: Rajni felt embarrassed and hurt, since the silence was because the laptop froze, not lack of interest.

qa.q: What did Rajni do that helped?
qa.a: Rajni emailed Mr Ghosh to explain, which led him to suggest using a hand emoji in the chat.

qa.q: How might Mr Ghosh see silence in video calls after Rajni's email?
qa.a: He might realise silence can mean technical problems, not lack of interest.

grounding: A teenager tells a friend how silence in an online class was misread as disinterest, and how digital tools helped.

passage:
My sister Binita's online class was on in the next room. Her camera was off, and I could see her through the doorway, sitting very still.
Then the teacher said, "Binita? Are you there?"
She didn't answer at first. I thought maybe she wasn't paying attention.
Then I saw her fingers flying on the keyboard. She typed "🙋 Sorry, lagging!" in the chat. A few seconds later, she unmuted and answered the question.
Later I asked her why she didn't just talk. She said, "Sometimes the sound cuts out, and I don't want to talk over someone."
I didn't know silence in online class could mean so many things.
- Chetan

qa.q: What did Binita type in the chat?
qa.a: "🙋 Sorry, lagging!"

qa.q: What might Binita have been feeling when the teacher called her name?
qa.a: She may have felt anxious and flustered, waiting for the lag to clear before she could answer.

qa.q: What did Binita do to take her turn without speaking over others?
qa.a: She used the chat and a hand emoji to show she was there before unmuting.

qa.q: How did Chetan see the silence at first?
qa.a: Chetan thought Binita wasn't paying attention, not realising it was lag.

grounding: An observer sees a teenager use a chat emoji to take a turn in an online class, learning silence can mean lag.

passage:
Monday: The first online class of flood week. Kiran unmuted to answer and talked straight over Ayesha, who had started at the same moment. Both stopped. Both started again. Ms Rao laughed. "Let's use the raise-hand button."
Wednesday: Kiran clicked the little hand and waited; when Ms Rao called on him, he unmuted, answered, and muted again. Ayesha's square stayed dark all class, and she didn't answer when called. Kiran wondered if she was bored, or still upset about Monday. After class he messaged her: "all ok? you went quiet." She replied: "power cut + my net keeps freezing. could hear only half."
Friday: Ayesha's connection held. She raised her hand, Kiran sent a 👍 in the chat when she finished, and nobody talked over anyone.

qa.q: Why was Ayesha quiet on Wednesday?
qa.a: There was a power cut and her net kept freezing, so she could hear only half.

qa.q: What was Kiran feeling about Ayesha's dark square?
qa.a: Kiran felt unsure and a little worried, wondering whether she was bored or still upset about Monday.

qa.q: What helped Kiran read Ayesha's silence fairly?
qa.a: He didn't assume; he messaged her privately to check, which showed the real reason was a power cut and lag.

qa.q: What was Wednesday's class like for Ayesha?
qa.a: Ayesha was probably frustrated, hearing only half the lesson on a freezing connection and unable to answer.

grounding: It shows a teenager using the raise-hand and mute tools to take turns online, and learning that silence in a video call can mean lag rather than disengagement.
